title: A biased allosteric modulator is a molecular glue for β2AR dimerization.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the only deposited coordinate file, PDB entry 9Q3L (583 KB mmCIF, a text format for atomic coordinates): 4,790 atoms, two receptor chains totalling 920 amino acids, 2.5 Angstrom cryo-EM (cryogenic electron microscopy) structure, with four small-molecule components (P0G, A1CNS, and two lipids C14 and LFA). Queried the RCSB Protein Data Bank by this paper's DOI and by PubMed ID: exactly one entry, no sibling depositions. Checked the linked map EMD-72202 by HEAD request: 176 MB gzip, over the 50 MB cap, so metadata only. Europe PMC reports the paper is not open access, not in PubMed Central, no supplementary files, no GEO/SRA/BioProject/dbGaP links, and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology and the experiments comes from the abstract alone: that AP-7-168 stabilises β2-adrenergic receptor homodimers, blocks β-arrestin coupling, enlarges nanoclusters in cells, and that 'extensive functional studies' were done. I could not see any of those functional measurements — the full text, supplementary tables and Nature Source Data files are behind a subscription and absent from PubMed Central.

a1_downloadable.note: The structure (PDB 9Q3L) and map (EMD-72202) download freely — I opened the mmCIF. But every tabular measurement the paper describes (dose-response curves, β-arrestin recruitment, bioluminescence resonance energy transfer dimerization assays) sits in paywalled supplementary/Source Data; Nature paper is subscription-only, not in PubMed Central, no Zenodo or Dryad deposit.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table anywhere, so no label column exists. Any prediction target (dimerization propensity, bias factor, interface residue) would have to be constructed from scratch by inference across the structure and outside sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs that do exist are complete and self-contained: the β2-adrenergic receptor sequence and coordinates are in the file, and the ligands are present as 3D chemical components, not just names.

a4_units_stated.note: The mmCIF carries standard units (Angstroms for coordinates, 2.5 Angstrom resolution). Not the issue here — there is simply nothing measured in units to predict.

a5_enough_rows.note: One deposited structure. Verified by two independent RCSB queries (by DOI and by PubMed ID 42618785) that no other entry belongs to this paper. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.6 MB coordinates; 176 MB map if needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small. Size was never the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked. The abstract says 'structures' (plural) and 'extensive functional studies', but only one structure is deposited and no functional numbers are visible, so I cannot reconcile the paper's claims with the files.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists to trace. If one were invented from this structure — e.g. 'is this residue in the dimer interface' — it would be computed directly from the input coordinates, which is leakage by construction, exactly the failure mode A8 is written to catch.

existing_models.name: GGIP (GPCR-GPCR Interaction Pair predictor), a support vector machine using amino-acid property scores
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved — I saw only the title and abstract summary in a search listing, not the paper.

existing_models.name: RosettaMPDock, a membrane-aware protein-protein docking method combined with AlphaFold3 structure prediction
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved — found as a 2025 conference abstract listing only.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would fit the receptor sequence, but there is nothing to fit it to
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice, if a dataset existed
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT; the paper itself is CC BY-NC-ND and paywalled

integration.partner_dataset: GPCRdb and the Protein Data Bank hold hundreds of G-protein-coupled receptor structures joinable on UniProt accession P07550 (β2-adrenergic receptor), and ChEMBL holds β2AR ligand activity data joinable on InChIKey.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: A join is conceivable — 'which receptor-ligand pairs form drug-glued dimers?' — but this paper contributes a single example to it, so the join would be entirely carried by the partner resource and not by this paper.

controls.positive_control: None available: with one structure there is no train/test anything.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable — label shuffling needs labels.
controls.external_validation: None attached to this paper. Other G-protein-coupled receptor dimer structures exist in the Protein Data Bank but were not produced by or linked to this work.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is possible from this paper's released data: it supports a single structural observation, not a prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use receptor sequence and ligand chemistry to predict which small molecules glue two copies of a receptor together.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model the amino-acid sequence of a G-protein-coupled receptor plus the chemical structure of a candidate drug. From this paper the number of examples is 1 (one receptor-ligand pair, verified in the deposited file).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the drug stabilises a receptor dimer and, if so, how strongly — the truth coming from biophysical assays such as bioluminescence resonance energy transfer or single-molecule imaging. Those measurements are in this paper's paywalled supplement and I never saw them.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Drug hunters at pharmaceutical companies and G-protein-coupled receptor labs would use a dimer-glue predictor to pick compounds worth testing, because 'molecular glue' is currently found by accident. But that project needs hundreds of measured ligand-receptor pairs, and this paper supplies one.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predicting ligand-induced G-protein-coupled receptor dimerization from receptor sequence plus ligand chemistry. The data for it does not exist here — this paper releases one cryo-EM structure of one receptor with one modulator. The structure is a valuable single data point for a future benchmark of membrane-protein docking methods (e.g. AlphaFold3 or RosettaMPDock asked to reproduce the transmembrane-helix 3/4/5 dimer interface), but a one-case benchmark is a figure, not a project.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the download: the single mmCIF is 583 KB with 4,790 atoms, so any computation on it is instantaneous. There is no cross-validation to time because there is nothing to cross-validate.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query the RCSB Protein Data Bank by the paper's DOI and count entries. It returns 1. That took one minute and settles it.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 outright: the paper's only openly released data is a single cryo-EM structure (PDB 9Q3L, 4,790 atoms, verified by opening the file), versus the ~1,500-row floor. Also fails A1 — the functional measurements that might have made a table are in Nature's paywalled Source Data, with no PubMed Central copy, no Zenodo/Dryad deposit and no repository accessions — and A2, since no prediction target is a column anywhere. Excellent structural biology, no machine-learning dataset.
